processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Raw materials with high purity (>99.9%) were melted to produce ingots with nominal composition Fe-35Mn-15Al-5Cu (at.%).
Homogenized ingots hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm.
Plates cut into 10 × 5 × 2 mm³ samples for Vickers hardness measurements and microstructure characterizations.
Solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under an argon atmosphere, followed by oil quenching.
Solution-treated samples aged at temperatures between 525 °C and 650 °C for 1, 3, 6 and 10 h, followed by water quenching. This sample corresponds to the 575 °C / 6 h condition.

structures.overall_structure: After aging at 575 °C for 6 h the 15Al (Fe-35Mn-15Al-5Cu, at.%) alloy has largely transformed from the α (BCC) matrix into the ultra-hard β-Mn phase, with fine new BCC and FCC Cu-rich precipitates distributed at the β-Mn interfaces; SE imaging of the 15Al alloy aged 575 °C/6 h shows a predominantly β-Mn matrix carrying an inset of fine needle-like precipitates.

phases_present.morphology: dominant matrix formed by α→β-Mn transformation; ultra-hard Mn-rich phase
fine precipitates at the β-Mn interfaces within the β-Mn
fine particles at the β-Mn interfaces, containing FCC twins

defect_interactions.interaction_type: FCC twins within the FCC Cu-rich particles
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: FCC twins were frequently observed within the fine FCC Cu-rich particles that form at the β-Mn interfaces.

interfaces.phase_evolution: α → α + FCC Cu-rich phase → α-Mn + β-Mn + BCC phase → β-Mn + BCC phase + FCC Cu-rich phase
interfaces.interface_notes: The paper reports that fine FCC Cu-rich particles and BCC particles form at the interfaces between the β-Mn; the BCC phase is attributed to enrichment of the BCC-stabilizing element Al around the β-Mn interfaces, and the Cu-rich phase to the limited solubility of Cu and its expulsion from β-Mn during precipitation/growth.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers microhardness of the 15Al alloy after aging at 575 °C for 6 h; load 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and the value is the average of 5 measurements.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: load 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times, hardness given by the average of 5 measurements
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the Vickers hardness of solution-treated and aged samples to map aging hardening behaviour.
characterization_methods.key_findings: The 15Al alloy aged at 575 °C for 6 h shows a Vickers hardness of 960.3 ± 6.8 HV (Table 2); overall hardness window of the 15Al alloy spans 253.4–965.6 HV.

characterization_methods.purpose: Identify phase compositions of the alloys.
characterization_methods.key_findings: For the 15Al alloy XRD (550 °C × 1 h) the pattern contains α/D0₃ together with α-Mn and β-Mn peaks, indicating α-Mn and β-Mn co-precipitation.

characterization_methods.technique: Scanning electron microscopy (SE) and energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS)
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ZEISS Sigma 300 SEM operated at 5 kV
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: secondary electron (SE) imaging of aged samples
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify the precipitation of secondary phases such as α-Mn and β-Mn in the aged samples.
characterization_methods.key_findings: SE images of the 15Al alloy show short rod-shaped β-Mn precipitating along α grain boundaries and within grains, growing until precipitates impinge; at high temperature/time the matrix appears essentially fully transformed.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: scanning step size 1.5 μm for low magnification and 0.05 μm for high magnification
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize the evolution of constituent phases (α, β-Mn, α-Mn, BCC, FCC) after different aging treatments.
characterization_methods.key_findings: Solution-treated alloys are single-phase α (BCC); after aging the α matrix progressively transforms into β-Mn with new BCC and FCC precipitates appearing at higher temperatures.

characterization_methods.technique: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) with SAED and EDS
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: FEI Talos F200X microscope equipped with an EDS detector, operated at 200 kV
characterization_methods.purpose: Elucidate the fine microstructures (β-Mn, FCC Cu-rich particles, twin structure) of alloys with ultra-high hardness.
characterization_methods.key_findings: In the aged 15Al alloy the fine particles at the β-Mn interfaces exhibit an FCC structure rich in Cu, depleted in Fe and Mn, with FCC twins frequently observed; β-Mn is poor in Cu.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: indentation depth 200 nm; test points spaced 5 μm or more apart
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure micro-hardness and the intrinsic hardness of β-Mn in the hardest samples.
characterization_methods.key_findings: For the hardest 15Al sample the average nanoindentation hardness was 11.7 ± 0.4 GPa, and the intrinsic hardness of β-Mn was 12.1 ± 0.3 GPa (measured on the 15Al peak-hardness, i.e. 600 °C/6 h, sample).

unmapped_findings: Sample identity: this sample is the Fe-35Mn-15Al-5Cu (at.%) "15Al" low-density steel (EDS composition Fe 44.6, Mn 35.2, Al 15.0, Cu 5.2 at.%; density 6.85 g·cm⁻³) after solution treatment at 1100 °C/10 min (oil quench) plus aging at 575 °C for 6 h followed by water quenching; its Vickers hardness is 960.3 ± 6.8 HV (Table 2).
Solution-treated baseline hardness of the 15Al alloy (parent state of this sample) is 253.4 ± 2.1 HV (Table 2, b0027/b0028).

NOT this sample (sibling): The fracture toughness K_IC = 8.6 MPa·m^1/2 and average crack length 18 μm reported for the 15Al alloy (b0061) were measured on the 15Al sample at peak hardness (965.6 HV), i.e. the 600 °C/6 h condition, NOT the 575 °C/6 h sample here.

NOT this sample (sibling): The nanoindentation average hardness 11.7 ± 0.4 GPa and the intrinsic β-Mn hardness 12.1 ± 0.3 GPa for 15Al (b0060) were measured on the 15Al hardest sample aged at 600 °C for 6 h (965.6 HV), not on the 575 °C/6 h sample.
NOT this sample (sibling): The β-Mn composition of the hardest 15Al sample (Mn 36.8, Al 14.3, Cu 2.8 at.%; Fig. 14/b0060) corresponds to the 600 °C/6 h peak-hardness condition.

NOT this sample (sibling): The ultra-high specific hardness of 141 HV·cm³/g reported for Fe-35.2Mn-15Al-5.2Cu (b0008, b0077) corresponds to the 15Al alloy at peak hardness (965.6 HV, 600 °C/6 h), not to the 575 °C/6 h condition.

Analytical model (Eq. 1, b0022): K_IC = 0.016 (E/HV)^(1/2) · P/c^(2/3), where E is the elastic modulus (164 GPa for 15Al), HV the Vickers hardness, P the indentation load (9.8 N) and c the average crack length (c = 0.25 Σ l_i). This model was applied only to the peak-hardness samples, not to the 575 °C/6 h sample.

The paper's EBSD maps of the 15Al alloy (Fig. 4) were acquired at 525 °C/3 h, 550 °C/6 h and 650 °C/3 h, and the 15Al XRD pattern (Fig. 10) at 550 °C/1 h; no EBSD/XRD was reported for the 15Al 575 °C/6 h condition specifically.
